title: Chapter 23
text: STARFISH In the sea rocks, in the stone pockets under the tide’s lip, in water dense as blindness they slid like sponges, like too many thumbs. I knew this, and what I wanted was to draw my hands back from the water — what I wanted was to be willing to be afraid. But I stayed there, I crouched on the stone wall while the sea poured its harsh song through the sluices, while I waited for the gritty lightning of their touch, while I stared down through the tide’s leaving where sometimes I could see them — their stubborn flesh lounging on my knuckles. What good does it do to lie all day in the sun loving what is easy? It never grew easy, but at last I grew peaceful: all summer my fear diminished as they bloomed through the water like flowers, like flecks of an uncertain dream, while I lay on the rocks, reaching into the darkness, learning little by little to love our only world.
